title: Responsiveness: mobile first, media queries and container queries

videos.script: The same page is opened on a phone in somebody's hand, on a laptop, and on a monitor as wide as a desk. {{three}} Nobody is going to build three sites for that. There is one page, and it has to work on all of them. {{earlier}} You have already seen layouts that adapt by themselves. A box with a maximum width. A row of covers that wraps. A grid that makes as many columns as fit. {{query}} This lesson adds the tool for the rest: the media query. It asks how wide the window is, and changes the layout when the answer is "narrow". {{first}} And it teaches an order to write things in. Start with the phone, the smallest and the hardest, and add to it as the screen grows. {{container}} Then a newer idea. A card does not care how wide the window is. It cares how much room it was given. Container queries let it ask that. {{prefs}} Width is not the only thing a reader can tell you. They can ask for less motion, or use a finger instead of a mouse. {{test}} And at the end, how to test all of it, down to a screen 320 pixels wide. {{close}}
